newsitem.title: USA: NYC club owner accused of tax evasion.
newsitem.headline: NYC club owner accused of tax evasion.

text.p: A New York City nightclub owner, accused last year of using the trendy hotspots to sell hallucinogenic drugs, was charged Wednesday with stealing more than $1 million in taxes as well, authorities said.

Peter Gatien, owner of the Limelight, the Tunnel and the Palladium, and his wife Alessandra Kobayashi Gatien were indicted on charges of grand larceny and violations of state and city tax laws, authorities said.
They also were charged with evading more than $250,000 in personal income taxes.

The couple is accused of paying $300,000 a year in personal expenses through corporations that operated the nightclubs and then claiming the expenses as business deductions, said Robert Morgenthau, Manhattan District Attorney.
He called it "a classic case of skimming," in which the club owner took cash collected as entry fees to the clubs and from the clubs' bars.

Last May, Gatien and 21 other people were arrested and charged with using the nightclubs to sell a hallucinogenic drug known as Ecstasy. Gatien and two top aides later were charged with cocaine distribution in the widening drug case.
Gatien has denied all the charges and is free on $1 million bond.
